description: Dashboard Attention Hero — a self-adaptive two-state view that mounts into the Dashboard Attention slot, renders shared attention items plus runner-down status, and offers direct navigate/Approve/Resume actions.

tasks.title: Implement Attention Hero widget and mount it in the Dashboard Attention slot
tasks.description: Add a new widget at packages/web/src/widgets/attention-hero/ exporting an AttentionHero component. It derives state exclusively from deriveAttentionItems(useIssues(), useAgentStatus()) with no local copy of the four attention rules, and renders two states: a has-attention state listing each AttentionItem (label + detail, in derivation order) with per-item direct actions (navigate to issue detail via useProjectPath; Approve via approveIssue for 'Approval needed' items; Resume via resumeIssue for Interrupted/Needs action/Integration failed items), plus a visually distinct Runner-down entry when agentStatus.runnerAvailable === false that links to /activity; and an all-clear state showing an 'All clear' message with a copy-only Productivity placeholder when no items and runner available. Wire AttentionHero into DashboardPage in place of DashboardZonePlaceholder for the attention slot only, preserving the data-testid="dashboard-zone-attention" / data-zone="attention" hook on the Hero root; the other three slots (Pulse/Productivity/Digest) remain placeholders. Reuse the IssueCard mutation pattern (invalidate ['issues'] + ['agent-status'] on success). Add unit tests for both states, per-item actions, runner-down entry (including the empty-items + runner-down case), all-clear, and the DashboardPage integration.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/web/src/widgets/attention-hero/ exports a public AttentionHero component with a full unit test suite.
AttentionHero imports deriveAttentionItems and AttentionItem from entities/issue and contains no local copy of any of the four attention rules (approval/integrate/interrupted/blocked).

When deriveAttentionItems returns a non-empty list, the Hero renders one entry per AttentionItem in evaluation order, each showing the item's label and detail, and does NOT render the all-clear state.
An AttentionItem whose label is 'Approval needed' exposes an Approve action that invokes approveIssue(issueNumber, projectId); activating it invalidates ['issues'] and ['agent-status'].

An AttentionItem whose underlying issue accepts a resume call (Interrupted/Needs action/Integration failed) exposes a Resume action that invokes resumeIssue(issueNumber, projectId); activating it invalidates ['issues'] and ['agent-status'].
Activating an entry's navigation affordance navigates to the issue detail route (issues/:number) via useProjectPath.

When agentStatus.runnerAvailable === false, the Hero renders a visually distinct Runner-down entry (even when deriveAttentionItems returns an empty list), showing agentStatus.runnerMessage ?? 'No runner is connected.' with a link to toProjectPath('/activity'), and does NOT render the all-clear state.
When agentStatus.runnerAvailable is true or undefined (loading), the Hero renders no Runner-down entry.

When deriveAttentionItems returns an empty list and agentStatus.runnerAvailable is not false, the Hero renders the all-clear state with an 'All clear' message and a copy-only Productivity placeholder (no live Productivity content, no extra fetches).
Surfacing an attention item triggers no notification, push, toast, or workflow-state mutation; mutations occur only on explicit user action.
DashboardPage renders AttentionHero in the Attention slot (not the generic placeholder); the Pulse, Productivity, and Digest slots still render DashboardZonePlaceholder.

The Attention Hero root carries data-testid="dashboard-zone-attention" and data-zone="attention" so existing zone-identity assertions remain meaningful; DashboardPage.test.tsx is updated to assert the Hero in the attention slot and placeholders in the other three.
Hero and Kanban produce identical attention items for the same (issues, agentStatus) input (verified by importing the same deriveAttentionItems).
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes, including the new widget tests and the updated DashboardPage tests.
tasks.output: packages/web/src/widgets/attention-hero/ (component + tests), updated packages/web/src/pages/dashboard/ui/DashboardPage.tsx and DashboardPage.test.tsx; typecheck + tests green; openspec validate issue-167 --strict green.
tasks.notes: Pure consumption UI — no server/domain changes. Reuse existing seams: useIssues (entities/issue), useAgentStatus (entities/agent), deriveAttentionItems/AttentionItem (entities/issue), approveIssue/resumeIssue (entities/issue/api/client), useProjectPath (entities/project). Reference patterns: KanbanBoard.tsx:542 (deriveAttentionItems usage), NeedsAttentionSummary (KanbanBoard.tsx:392), RunnerUnavailableBanner (KanbanBoard.tsx:449), IssueCard.tsx:203 (resume mutation + invalidation). Per spec, key Runner-down off agentStatus.runnerAvailable === false (treats undefined/loading as available); note Kanban's banner uses useRunnerSummary().hasConnectedCapacity — this divergence is an accepted trade-off, not a bug. Also satisfies the dashboard-shell MODIFIED requirement (Attention slot hosts the Hero; other three slots remain placeholders).
